thesis: LiveRamp is under a definitive agreement to be acquired by Publicis Groupe for $38.50 per share in cash. Closing is expected by the end of calendar 2026, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The stock closed at $38.51 on 3.3x volume, at the deal price, so upside appears capped. A consumer privacy class action (Riganian v. LiveRamp, N.D. Cal.) is in discovery, with class certification expected to be decided in late 2026. This run found no restatement.
invalidation: The deal breaks or a higher bid emerges.

thesis: AvePoint traded 10.7x volume today and slipped about 1.6% to $17.08, near its 52-week high. This run found no company announcement explaining the volume. The most recent company news is an Oct 27 product launch (the AvePoint Trust Platform), and Q3 results are due Nov 5 against a revenue guidance range ($128.2-130.2M) that sits below the ~$133.6M consensus. With the driver unidentified and a binary report days away, the read is unresolved. A 2025 Delaware settlement ($14.4M) over the SPAC-era proxy is closed, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: A disclosed catalyst for the volume, or Q3 results on Nov 5 that beat the consensus.

thesis: LXP Industrial Trust is being acquired by Brookfield and CPP Investments for $61.20 per share in cash. Shareholders approved the deal on Oct 26 with over 99% of votes cast, and closing is expected Nov 2, after which the shares will be delisted. At $61.175 the stock sits at the deal price, so upside is capped. One complaint and 14 demand letters alleged proxy disclosure deficiencies; the company supplemented its proxy and denies the claims. This run found no restatement.

Global Payments rose about 13.1% today to $96.98 on 8.4x volume, a 52-week high, after a report that Clayton Dubilier & Rice is pursuing a take-private of the company. No offer, price, financing or agreement has been confirmed, and Q3 results are due in early November. The move rests on an unconfirmed report, so the read is unresolved. The June 2026 10-Q describes only routine claims; an earlier securities class action over the Active Network unit reached a preliminary settlement. This run found no restatement.
invalidation: A signed, company-announced transaction with disclosed terms.

thesis: Bausch Health fell about 7.9% today to $8.21 on 2.4x volume, giving back part of its two-day post-earnings run, and this run found no new disclosure explaining the dip. The Oct 28 Q3 report (PR Newswire) showed revenue of $2.94B, adjusted EPS of $1.77 against ~$1.27 expected, and a second straight full-year guidance raise. The counter-cases are structural and unresolved, which caps this at medium. Debt is roughly $20B with liabilities exceeding assets, and Xifaxan faces a Medicare price change hitting Q4 and loss of exclusivity in 2028. A 2023 securities class action over the Bausch + Lomb spinoff has no scheduled ruling identified.
invalidation: Cash flow or debt reduction stalls, guidance is cut on the Xifaxan Medicare pricing change, or an adverse Xifaxan exclusivity development.

thesis: ADT is under a definitive agreement (Oct 29, 2026, 8-K) to be acquired by Thrive Holdings for $10.00 per share in cash. Financing comes from Apollo-managed funds, closing is expected in Q1 2027, and a go-shop runs through Nov 28 with a possible 10-day extension. The stock was flat at $9.87 on 3.7x volume, about 1.3% below the deal price, so upside appears capped barring a topping bid. This run found no deal-related lawsuit filed.
invalidation: A topping bid above $10.00 during the go-shop period.

thesis: CBIZ is being acquired by a Grant Thornton affiliate backed by New Mountain Capital for $55.00 per share in cash. Stockholders approved the deal on Oct 27, and closing is expected on or about Nov 2. At $54.99 the stock sits at the deal price, so upside is capped. A valuation-fraud suit by a former AmeriTex CFO (Podlasek v. CBIZ, S.D. Tex.) is in discovery. A single low-reliability source reports a revised Q1 2026 result and a material weakness, which this run could not confirm in a filing.

Newell Brands reported Q3 2026 today (8-K). Net sales rose 3.7% to about $1.9B (core +3.3%), normalized EPS was $0.20 against $0.17 a year earlier, and the full-year sales outlook was raised. However, a $101M tradename impairment produced a GAAP loss of $0.19 per share, and coverage cites a sharp operating-margin drop and persistent inflation. The shares fell about 7% premarket before closing up about 2.0% at $5.18. The results are mixed, and leverage remains high, with debt reduction of only a couple hundred million dollars planned this year. The 2023 SEC settlement over sales disclosures falls just outside the 3-year window.
invalidation: Q4 results show margins recovering alongside sales growth, with debt reduction on track.

thesis: Repligen reported Q3 2026 on Oct 27 (8-K). Revenue rose 11% to $209M (12.5% organic), adjusted EPS of $0.53 beat ~$0.46, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $844-852M; the BioLife Solutions acquisition closed Oct 6. The stock fell about 6.2% today to $176.94 on 3.4x volume. The quarter also included an intangible-asset impairment, and the Q3 10-Q refers to material weaknesses in internal control. The company completed a restatement on Nov 18, 2024 over the timing of revenue from a COVID-related cancellation payment, which falls inside the 3-year window and flags governance history.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the raised guidance, or further control or accounting issues.

thesis: Kenvue traded 3.2x volume today and slipped about 1.5% to $19.275. Its pending acquisition by Kimberly-Clark was approved by shareholders in January 2026, and Kimberly-Clark raised $4.9B of senior notes on Oct 29 to fund it. Reports conflict on whether closing and delisting are imminent, with primary filings still describing closing as expected in Q4 2026. Kenvue also faces revived Tylenol autism litigation: the Second Circuit reinstated more than 500 cases in July and denied rehearing on Oct 16, and the company says it will seek Supreme Court review. The outcome is driven by deal timing and that litigation, so the read is unresolved.
invalidation: The acquisition closes as scheduled, or a favorable Supreme Court outcome in the Tylenol litigation.

thesis: ResMed fell about 9.0% today to $230.12 on 3.1x volume after reporting fiscal Q1 2027 on Oct 29 (8-K). Revenue rose 6% to $1.4B, GAAP diluted EPS rose 23% to $2.92 and non-GAAP EPS 14% to $2.91, and the company returned more than $1.0B through buybacks and dividends. This run found no explanation for the selloff, so the read is unresolved: the stock is falling despite solid reported growth. Patent litigation with Cleveland Medical is pending on appeal, and the 2024 Class I mask-magnet recall is older. This run found no restatement or new investigation.
invalidation: A disclosed reason for the selloff that leaves the growth outlook intact, or the next quarter confirming the trend.

thesis: Estee Lauder traded 3.0x volume today and closed about 0.4% higher at $109.23, ahead of fiscal Q1 2027 results on Nov 2, a pending binary event, with no company-specific news identified for today. The company has guided to a raised fiscal 2027 adjusted operating margin of 12.7-13.5% and stronger first-half growth. Its $210M securities class action settlement awaits final court approval, and a board committee is reviewing related stockholder derivative demands. This run found no restatement.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 results on Nov 2 confirm the margin outlook and first-half growth.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). AVTR fell about 3.7% today to $16.06, now about 2.7% below the $16.51 average cost, and closed below its 20-day average (about $16.27). That meets one of the invalidation criteria named in the prior thesis, and this run found no new company disclosure that would offset it. The Oct 28 Q3 report (8-K) was a beat-and-raise: 5.2% organic growth, adjusted EPS of $0.22, and higher 2026 guidance. But adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS still fell year over year, the motion to dismiss the securities class action remains unresolved, and the stock has sold off since the report. With its own invalidation met, the thesis no longer supports holding. The opening buy was 9 trading days ago, outside the 5-day early-exit window.
invalidation: A recovery back above the 20-day average on evidence of margin improvement.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF closed flat at $14.26, above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M against $575M guidance, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. The outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, and the Hamilton (Stelco) layoffs confirmed Oct 21 point to tariff pressure on the Canadian unit. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV slipped about 1.7% to $36.89, above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 21-22 CLARITY Phase 3 results for brepocitinib in non-infectious uveitis, a drug already approved for dermatomyositis. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 26). RNG fell about 2.8% to $81.37, still above the ~$79.42 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 22 Q3 2026 report (8-K). Revenue rose 5.9% to $676M, above the $664-670M guidance, and the non-GAAP operating margin reached 24.7%, up about 190bp. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.650-2.657B in revenue, $5.07-5.12 in non-GAAP EPS and $620-630M in free cash flow. ARR from customers using a paid AI product doubled to nearly 15% of the total. The strongest counter-case is competitive: growth is only about 6% in a crowded cloud-communications market. That doesn't change the read, because the beat, the margin expansion and the raised EPS and free-cash-flow guidance all come from the company's own disclosed results at that growth rate. This is the counter-case named and resolved in the prior thesis, and no new fact reopens it. A January 2026 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, the 10-Q shows no material proceeding, and the next earnings report is about four months away (Feb 2027).
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margin falls short of the raised guidance, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$79.42).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28). Centene slipped about 0.2% to $68.47, still just above its ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 27 Q3 report (8-K): adjusted EPS of $0.58 against a consensus near $0.07-0.10, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to above $5.20, and Medicare Advantage now expected to break even in 2026. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and cap this at medium. Medicaid margins are pressured (93.6% benefits ratio), with management expecting membership declines and acuity shifts to slow recovery through 2027, and the company also plans to exit Arkansas's Medicaid expansion in 2027. The GAAP loss of $0.14 per share is not attributed to a specific charge. A securities class action (Lunstrum v. Centene, S.D.N.Y.) has no scheduled ruling identified.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or the stock falls back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
